subject: difficulty with data named alpha or beta or gamma

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: difficulty with data named alpha or beta or gamma
parts:
Hi, is there some sort of rule in Stan that you can't give the names alpha or beta or gamma to data? I don't recall such a rule but I'm having problems here.

Here's what happened (after I stripped down the problem to its essentials).

Here's the Stan program:

data {
real alpha;
}
parameters {
real theta;
}
model {
theta ~ normal(alpha, 1);
}

And here's the R code:

alpha <- 2
fit_2 <- stan("beta_test_2.stan")

And here's the R output:

Error in new_CppObject_xp(fields$.module, fields$.pointer, ...) :
variable does not exist; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=alpha; base type=double
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In is.na(x) : is.na() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'closure'
2: In FUN(X[[i]], ...) : data with name alpha is not numeric and not used
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done

When I call the data "beta" or "gamma" I also get an error. But when I call the data "a" or "b" or "alpha0" or "beta0" or "gamma0" it runs just fine.

It only seems like a problem with data, not with parameters. The following works, where I switch things around and let alpha be the name of a parameter:

data {
real a;
}
parameters {
real alpha;
}
model {
alpha ~ normal(a, 1);
}

This is a problem. It might seem like no big deal--just don't use alpha, beta, gamma as data--but we often use these as parameter names, and when debugging it can be useful to take a parameter declaration and put it in data (that is, running a model setting a certain parameter as fixe).

So I'm not sure what's going on here. I guess it could be an issue not with Stan but with Rstan; I don't know.

I'm running R 3.3.1 and rstan 2.12.1.

Thanks for your help.
Andrew

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] difficulty with data named alpha or beta or gamma
parts:
Hi Andrew,

It looks like there's an issue where RStan is pulling alpha from the global environment, which is a function, not the value you set.

> ?alpha
Help on topic ‘alpha’ was found in the following packages:
  Package               Library
  scales                /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.3/Resources/library
  ggplot2               /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.3/Resources/library

If you pass data into the stan() function, it works fine:
> fit_2 <- stan("beta_test_2.stan", data = list(alpha = 2))
or even:
fit_2 <- stan("beta_test_2.stan", data = list(alpha = alpha))

I don't know enough about how RStan grabs things out of the global environment to tell if this can be dealt with automatically, but the current workaround is to pass data into the Stan call.



Daniel
